profile.background: A 43-year-old adult lives with a partner, works part time in a print shop, and keeps score for a weekend softball league.
profile.history: In outpatient follow-up for schizophrenia after a hospital stay four years ago. Has taken the same evening prescription for over a year.
profile.organization: Keeps events in sequence. Distinguishes day-to-day observations from memories of being unwell.
profile.spontaneity: Conversational about work and leisure. A detail about a recent change often comes to mind while describing a routine.
profile.guardedness: Comfortable discussing treatment in clinic. More private about the hospital stay.
profile.expression: Easy conversational rhythm with dry humor about minor inconveniences. Usually speaks in a few connected sentences. Gives a shorter reply to a narrow factual question.
profile.self_understanding: Remembers how convincing earlier experiences felt. Uses sleep and concentration as personal indicators of how the week is going.

facts.content: Opens the print shop with a coworker on three mornings each week.
Takes the prescribed tablet with supper. The morning alarm is still hard to get up for on some days.
facts.disclosure_context: Medication routine and how mornings feel.

facts.content: The main recent sleep change was waking earlier on two nights while the apartment upstairs was being painted.
Can follow a softball game from beginning to end, including keeping track of substitutions.
Before the hospital stay, announcements over a store speaker seemed to comment on personal purchases. That has not happened in the past year.
A coworker switched opening days last week so the patient could get to a morning appointment.
Feels steady enough to take on one extra shift, though wants to keep Sunday free for the league.
facts.disclosure_context: Work goals and how to spend the weekend.

profile.background: A 32-year-old adult shares an apartment with an older cousin and enjoys solving crossword puzzles with a pen.
profile.history: Receives outpatient care for schizophrenia. A frightening period of hearing a stranger speaking in an empty room ended about ten months ago.
profile.organization: Follows a question and keeps one idea distinct from another. No recent difficulty finding the names of familiar things.
profile.spontaneity: Rarely starts a new subject. Takes time to decide what to say even with familiar people.
profile.guardedness: Generally comfortable here. Remembers being embarrassed to tell the cousin about hearing a voice.
profile.expression: Quiet, even voice. More animation when describing a difficult crossword clue. Often answers in a phrase or one short sentence. Can give a concrete detail about an event.
profile.self_understanding: Feels the hardest part lately is starting an activity. Enjoyment often comes back once the activity is underway.

facts.content: Keeps the newspaper crossword folded on the kitchen table and does it after lunch several days a week.
facts.disclosure_context: Daily interests and ways of spending time.

facts.content: Deciding to go outside takes effort. Once out walking, usually enjoys the river path.
Went out for bread on Tuesday after the cousin asked, then took the long way by the river.
Attends the clinic for a scheduled injection and keeps the next appointment on a paper calendar.
The arm can ache the evening after an injection and usually feels fine the next morning.
The last time the unfamiliar voice was heard was about ten months ago. Speaking about it still feels embarrassing.
facts.disclosure_context: Questions about hearing things and personal reactions.

facts.content: Would like to make one trip outside each week by choice. Thinks choosing the destination the night before might help.

profile.background: A 37-year-old adult works at an alterations counter and lives alone. Experiments with bread recipes on days off.
profile.history: Attends outpatient care for schizophrenia. An occasional voice has continued during otherwise fairly steady months on medication.
profile.organization: Recounts events chronologically and distinguishes the sound, the interpretation, and what happened next.
profile.spontaneity: Generally starts with the most recent relevant event. Happy to talk about sewing or baking.
profile.guardedness: Cautious about discussing the voice because of a past awkward conversation with a friend.
profile.expression: Measured conversational pace. Occasionally stops to clarify a word that could give the wrong impression. Usually offers a short connected account. Can explain a particular episode in greater detail.
profile.self_understanding: Has considered several explanations for the voice and remains unsure. Knows the experience is more distracting after work than during it.

facts.content: Repairs hems and zippers at work. Listening to a radio show while making dough is a favorite evening activity.
Two evenings last week, heard a voice say “too slow” while sorting sewing supplies at home. It did not give any directions.
facts.disclosure_context: Hearing an unexpected sound or voice.

facts.content: Sometimes wonders whether a neighbor is speaking through the wall. Also remembers hearing it once when that apartment was vacant.
facts.disclosure_context: Interpretation of the sound and degree of certainty.

facts.content: Turning on the radio can make the sound less distracting. It is still possible to finish sorting thread.
facts.disclosure_context: Effects on a task and how the evening continues.

facts.content: Takes prescribed medication before bed. Remembers the evening dose by putting the unopened packet near the toothbrush.
Closed the alterations counter with a coworker on Friday and finished all the tickets before going home.
facts.disclosure_context: Recent workday and ability to finish tasks.

facts.content: The sound has not interrupted a conversation with a customer this month.

profile.background: A 51-year-old adult lives in a studio and grows herbs on the fire escape. Visits a sister in the same neighborhood.
profile.history: Followed in an outpatient clinic for schizophrenia. At a stressful point last winter, several familiar voices seemed to overlap. The experience is now infrequent.
profile.organization: One detail can call up a loosely related memory before the original point is finished. Usually recalls the question and can return to it.
profile.spontaneity: Likes to tell stories about the neighborhood. Sometimes needs a moment to pick one of several recent events.
profile.guardedness: Comfortable discussing daily life and clinic care. Hesitant about the strain last winter put on the relationship with the sister.
profile.expression: Friendly and expressive. An aside can interrupt an otherwise understandable account. Moderately talkative. Uses several short clauses or a short anecdote about a familiar activity.
profile.self_understanding: Notices that conversations get harder to follow when tired. Can describe how sleep and evening company feel different.

facts.content: Walks to the sister’s flat most Saturdays and trades herbs for leftovers.
Has started waking once around dawn on some mornings, then usually gets back to sleep.
Last heard the overlapping voices about three weeks ago in the evening while alone.
On the last visit, the sister set aside a basil pot and the two of them repotted it after lunch.
facts.disclosure_context: A recent visit or an activity done together.

facts.content: Picks up a box of tablets from the pharmacy every four weeks. Has the refill date written inside the kitchen cupboard.
Can lose the thread of a family conversation when tired. Repotting the plant with the sister felt easy.
facts.disclosure_context: Attention in conversations and practical tasks.

facts.content: Thinks a shorter afternoon visit fits current energy better than staying through dinner.

profile.background: A 46-year-old adult lives alone, works two afternoons a week shelving donated books, and likes old travel maps.
profile.history: In outpatient treatment for schizophrenia. During an episode two years ago, people on buses sometimes seemed to be talking about the patient.
profile.organization: Accurate about recent activities and shifts between topics easily when a question changes.
profile.spontaneity: Usually waits to be invited into a conversation. Has felt this way even on relatively good days.
profile.guardedness: The work schedule and prescription feel ordinary to discuss. Past feelings of being talked about are private.
profile.expression: Low-key speaking voice with few changes in emphasis. Expresses enjoyment plainly when discussing maps. A few words or a short sentence are typical. Has details readily available about a recent shift.
profile.self_understanding: Recognizes that the bus experience no longer has the same hold. Getting ready to leave home still takes time.

facts.content: Shelves donated books on Wednesday and Friday afternoons. The history shelves are closest to the sorting table.
Can lose nearly half an hour sitting with shoes on before leaving for a shift. Once inside the shop, sorting goes smoothly.
facts.disclosure_context: Getting ready for work and settling in.

facts.content: On Friday found an old railway atlas in a donation box and set it aside for the map shelf.
facts.disclosure_context: A concrete event at work or interest in maps.

facts.content: Takes a tablet after the evening meal. The outpatient nurse calls once a month to check how things are going.
Two years ago strangers chatting on buses seemed to be discussing the patient. Has not had that feeling on recent trips.
facts.disclosure_context: Experiences on public transit, past and recent.

facts.content: Still finds the midday bus quieter and usually takes it to the shop.
facts.disclosure_context: Travel preferences and current bus rides.

facts.content: Would like to leave home ten minutes earlier for work to have time to look at the map display before a shift.

profile.background: A 55-year-old adult shares a home with a friend, helps at a community kitchen, and listens to recorded detective stories.
profile.history: Seen as an outpatient for schizophrenia. During an episode several years ago, ordinary radio broadcasts took on personal significance. Has felt well this past year.
profile.organization: Tells a clear account and uses dates or recurring events as time markers.
profile.spontaneity: Readily volunteers a mundane practical detail when talking about food or appointments.
profile.guardedness: Comfortable with most topics. Describes the old episode briefly because it was upsetting.
profile.expression: Warm and matter-of-fact, with more energy when discussing a recipe. Talks in short paragraphs about routines and uses a sentence for most straightforward factual questions.
profile.self_understanding: Has learned that losing track of everyday tasks for several days is a reason to check in with the clinic. Occasional forgetfulness feels ordinary.

facts.content: Labels leftovers every Thursday at the community kitchen and brings a recorded mystery for the walk there.
Can follow most of a mystery on a walk. On a noisy corner, sometimes rewinds when a line is missed.
Takes the prescribed tablet in the morning. A pill organizer sits next to the kettle.
A dry mouth is most noticeable halfway through the kitchen shift. Usually brings a water bottle.
facts.disclosure_context: Discomfort during the day and treatment concerns.

facts.content: Several years ago radio weather reports seemed meant personally. Has listened to broadcasts without that feeling over the past year.
facts.disclosure_context: Previous experiences with broadcasts and how they feel currently.

facts.content: At the last kitchen shift, noticed the stew had no date label and checked with the cook before putting it away.
facts.disclosure_context: A recent shift and steps in a kitchen task.

facts.content: Wants to keep the current number of kitchen shifts because long afternoons leave little time for listening at home.

profile.background: A 29-year-old adult lives with a sibling, repairs bicycles as a hobby, and attends a part-time adult education course.
profile.history: Attends an outpatient service for schizophrenia. Voices that used to interrupt reading have become much less frequent. Still finds it hard to keep a train of thought when several things compete for attention.
profile.organization: Can drift from a question to a related detail, especially when two situations are compared. The connection is usually understandable.
profile.spontaneity: Talkative about how things are made and less forthcoming about personal experiences.
profile.guardedness: Comfortable describing the clinic routine. Past experiences in class feel a little embarrassing.
profile.expression: Thoughtful tone, sometimes breaks off briefly and resumes a thought from a different angle. Often speaks in a few linked phrases, occasionally adding a short aside.
profile.self_understanding: Notices that a physical task is easier to return to than a page of reading. Can describe the difference in everyday terms.

facts.content: Takes a geography class on Tuesday evenings and keeps a borrowed bicycle repair stand by the apartment door.
Reading in a room with conversation makes it easy to lose the place on the page. In a quiet library it is easier.
Straightened a bent mudguard last weekend after the sibling had trouble with a wheel rubbing.
facts.disclosure_context: A recent practical task and home routine.

facts.content: Last noticed a voice saying a single name about a month ago, at home. It has not interrupted the last few classes.
facts.disclosure_context: Recent voices and experiences in class.

facts.content: Takes a prescribed evening tablet and has been practicing ways to manage distractions with a clinic worker.
Using a slip of paper below the current line helped finish a short passage for class last week.
Likes the course and wants to do more of the reading before class rather than on the trip there.

profile.background: A 40-year-old adult lives with a housemate, works mornings at a garden center, and draws buildings in a small sketchbook.
profile.history: Receives outpatient care for schizophrenia. Has continued to notice occasional looks from people in public that can feel personally significant.
profile.organization: Describes observations, worries, and subsequent events in an orderly sequence. Able to consider uncertainty without losing the original point.
profile.spontaneity: Speaks freely about drawing and work. Usually gives a general description before a personal example.
profile.guardedness: Worries that other people might find the concerns about strangers strange. More comfortable discussing what happened than what it might mean.
profile.expression: Clear, measured speech. Sounds uneasy when describing being singled out. Typically gives a few connected sentences and can be concise on routine matters.
profile.self_understanding: Knows that strangers may be looking past the patient. Even with that possibility in mind the moment can feel uncomfortable.

facts.content: Works morning shifts at a garden center and draws storefronts in a sketchbook after work.
At a bus shelter on Monday, two people looked up at the same time. Felt singled out and moved to the other end of the shelter.
facts.disclosure_context: Feeling noticed or singled out in public.

facts.content: Wondered if the people had recognized the patient, but also wondered if they were looking for the bus. Remains uncertain.
facts.disclosure_context: Making sense of other people’s looks.

facts.content: Waited at the same shelter on Wednesday without feeling watched. The Monday experience still comes to mind occasionally.
facts.disclosure_context: Variation across trips and recent worries.

facts.content: Takes medication in the evening and talks to a clinic counselor about how the week has gone every other Friday.
Completed a sketch of the corner grocery last weekend and took it home to add the window frames.
It feels easier to concentrate on a drawing at home than at a busy stop where people stand close by.
